claims.event: After defeating Yelü Xie Shi with 2,500 men, decreed that 300 households form a mouke and ten mouke a meng'an.
Liao commander defeated by Emperor Taizu with twenty-five hundred men in the second year of his reign.
Liao subject given command of a mouke formed from 130 northern households.
Han subject given command of a mouke of sixty-five Han households from various prefectures.
Led his own followers organized as a separate meng'an alongside Gao Congyou.
Led his own followers organized as a separate meng'an alongside Wang Bolong.
After Pingzhou was pacified in Tianhui 2, abolished the meng'an system for surrendered peoples, fearing mixed customs.
In Huangtong 5 abolished hereditary meng'an and mouke among Liaodong Han and Bohai and graded the units into three tiers.
In Tiande 2 consolidated frontier commands and meng'an units and abolished the three grades.
His meng'an was moved from the Upper Capital circuit to the Central Capital as a hezha meng'an in the Zhenyuan relocation.
His meng'an was moved from the Upper Capital circuit to the Central Capital as a hezha meng'an in the Zhenyuan relocation.
Right Remonstrator whose meng'an was resettled at the Central Capital in the Zhenyuan relocation.
Grand Preceptor whose clan was resettled at the Central Capital in the Zhenyuan relocation.
Clansman whose kin were resettled at the Central Capital in the Zhenyuan relocation.
State duke whose meng'an was resettled in Shandong after the Zhenyuan capital relocation.
State duke whose meng'an was resettled in Shandong after the Zhenyuan capital relocation.
State duke whose meng'an was resettled in Shandong after the Zhenyuan capital relocation.
Grand Guardian whose meng'an was resettled in Shandong after the Zhenyuan capital relocation.
Household Master whose meng'an was resettled in Shandong after the Zhenyuan capital relocation.
Assistant to the State whose meng'an was resettled in Shandong after the Zhenyuan capital relocation.
Dingyuan officer whose meng'an was resettled in Shandong after the Zhenyuan capital relocation.
Late Duke of Guo whose meng'an was resettled in Shandong after the Zhenyuan capital relocation.
His clan was resettled in the Northern Capital after the Zhenyuan capital relocation.
His kinsmen were resettled in Hejian after the Zhenyuan capital relocation.
In Zhenglong 2 ordered to assign the old armies to command offices and grant them fields and cattle.
Installed as emperor at the Eastern Capital by soldiers returning from Daming.
His rebellion was suppressed at the start of the Dading era, after which the Khitan were dispersed among meng'an units.
In Dading 15 sent with nine others across the realm to re-register meng'an and mouke households.
Replied to the emperor that the northern lands could not be farmed, so rotating garrison duty was necessary.
Repeatedly urged settling poor households permanently on the frontier with state grain, and was praised by the emperor.
In Dading 21 dispatched to relocate two meng'an of the Hebei East Route among Jurchen households.
Ordered to inspect the Yaoluo River meng'an lands and arrange mixed settlement.
Explained that Shandong colonists treated granted land as home and lived apart even from brothers, causing poverty.
Proposed requiring separated brothers among the Shandong colonists to farm together again.
In Dading 23 relocated eight mouke of the Shandong East Route to Hejian.
Had wished to relocate the Suifen and Huligai peoples but failed to do so.
In Dading 24 disbursed treasury funds to move Suifen and Huligai meng'an to the Upper Capital lands.

label.en: Director of the Ministry of Personnel

claims.event: In the Mingchang era ordered meng'an and mouke to present jinshi candidates tested in policy essays and archery, and created the Loyalty Armies.
Compiled the Military Canon, which the emperor read and judged hard to put into practice.
Told the emperor that fixed manual methods fail in changing conditions and that the dynasty used regular and extraordinary forces.
Xi leader whose nine meng'an formed the Xi Army.
In Dading 17 renamed the capital city-defense force the Martial Guard Army.
Surrendered to the Jin in the Tianhui era with the Ever-Victorious Army of Liao River men.
Ordered the homesick Ever-Victorious Army of Guo Yaoshi disbanded and sent home.
A surviving Han army still bore the name of Han Chang after the Zhenglong disbandments.
When he moved the court south, the zhan armies collapsed and meng'an households were driven across the river.
Liu Qi of Hunyuan condemned the Jin general draft for stripping households of every able-bodied man.
In the Zhenyou era, enraged by protesting drafted clerks, ordered attendants to drive them off with bows and arrows.
Former attendant censor nearly sixty years old who was drafted as a qianhu at Xuzhou in the Yuanguang draft.
Liu Qi's father, a former surveillance censor, drafted as a qianhu at Chenzhou in the Yuanguang draft.
In Zhengda 2 his court proposed selecting elite troops from every circuit to serve directly under the Privy Council.
One of the first six commandants promoted, serving as Jianwei commandant at the capital in the Tianxing era.
One of the first six commandants promoted, serving as Zhechong commandant at Xuzhou in the Tianxing era.
One of the first six commandants promoted, serving as Zhenwu commandant at Chenzhou in the Tianxing era.
One of the first six commandants promoted, serving as Dangkou commandant at Caizhou in the Tianxing era.
One of the first six commandants promoted, posted to Shenyu and Anping in the Tianxing era.
One of the first six commandants promoted, serving as Zhenwu commandant in the Song and Ru region.
Later appointed Huwei commandant at Jinchang Prefecture in the Tianxing era.
Later appointed Guoyi commandant with acting authority at Guide in the Tianxing era.
Later appointed Tiankou commandant at the Southern Capital in the Tianxing era.
Assigned as Huben acting commandant at Tongguan in the Tianxing era.
Inner-clan member assigned as Yingyang acting commandant at Tongguan.
One of three acting commandants assigned to Tongguan in the Tianxing era.
Placed in overall command of the Loyal and Filial Army of guizheng men with Pucha Dingzhu.
Placed in overall command of the Loyal and Filial Army of guizheng men with Shimo Yanshannu.
Inner-clan officer who led three thousand imperial guards at the great muster at the Caomen drill ground.
Led four thousand men at the great muster at the Caomen drill ground under Emperor Aizong.
Selected the troops mustered at Caomen while holding direct control of the Privy Council.
Northern envoy murdered on their own authority by the Loyal Righteous Army, hastening the fall of the Jin.
His forces were reorganized as hezha meng'an of the Palace Guard Personal Army at the Zhenyuan relocation.
His forces were reorganized as hezha meng'an of the Palace Guard Personal Army at the Zhenyuan relocation.
His forces were reorganized as hezha meng'an of the Palace Guard Personal Army at the Zhenyuan relocation.
Renamed the Upper Capital Dragon Soaring Army the Divine Valor Army.
In Chengan 4 increased the Upper Capital garrison guard to five thousand and then six thousand.
Target of the Xianzhou Army Marshal Bureau set up in Shouguo 1 to secure Liao territory.
Target of the Southern Route Chief Command Bureau set up in Shouguo 1.
In Tianhui 1 split the Southwest Chief Command Office into Southwest and Northwest Route offices.
In Tiande 2 converted the capitals' Chief Deployment Offices into route chief command prefectures.
At the founding granted hereditary wanhu titles to able commanders, as recalled in the edict abolishing the office.
During Taihe ordered a branch of the Northeast Pacification Bureau established at Jinshan, nearer the frontier.
In Zhenyou 3 mobilized the Daizhou garrison, and in Xingding 1 fixed rewards for civilians surrendering lost army horses.
Advised that the five thousand Daizhou garrison troops be kept at Dai to shield Pingyang, and his advice was followed.
Established seven herd offices including Teman, Tetman, Woduzhi and Pusuwan.
In Tianjuan 3 issued an edict granting graded annual silk allotments to the Liaodong garrison troops.
His Dading 3 southern campaign gave rise to military expense funds, and he rebuked the marshal's office for levying the people.
In Xingding 2 objected that households with no soldier or adult men still drew army rations.
In Xingding 5 warned that 400,000 garrison household members consumed over 1.4 million shi of grain a year from civilian rent.

label.en: Military Commissioner of the Zhanghua Army
